## Triage (04 Nov 2026)

### REAL: RBA raises cash rate to 4.85% (3 Nov 2026)
- **What happened:** Reserve Bank of Australia lifted the cash rate to 4.85%. Reports say it is the fifth hike of 2026, an 18-year high, on a 6-3 split vote. The decision was expected (hence the "no-surprise" headline; the keyword match itself was a false hit). Source: RBA Monetary Policy Board statement https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html ; Babypips https://www.babypips.com/news/headline-rba-interest-rate-decision-november-2026-fifth-hike-split-vote . Figures are leads until fact-checked against the RBA statement.
- **Why several countries care:** Australia's variable-rate mortgages feel it almost at once. Australia is now hiking while other central banks hold or cut, and that gap moves the AUD and shows up in every viewer's import prices and travel money. The Bank of England decides tomorrow (5 Nov) and Canada's budget is tabled the same day, which gives a natural "same week, different directions" comparison.
- **Evergreen question:** How does a central bank's rate rise actually reach your mortgage, your savings and your currency, and why are countries moving in opposite directions?
- **Working title:** "Australia Just Raised Rates Again. Why Is Everyone Else Cutting?"
- **Fit:** Standalone explainer. It could include a Dollar Yardstick segment comparing mortgage payments on the same loan in AU/UK/US/CA.
- **Speed:** Within a month. It was expected, so there is no breaking-news rush. Pair it with tomorrow's BoE result if that diverges.
